```{r setup, include=FALSE}

library(flexdashboard)
library(DT)
library(dplyr)
library(htmltools)
library(bslib)

# data
mode_effects <- readRDS("mode_effects.RDS")
studies_info <- readRDS("studies_info.RDS")
```

Intro
=====================================

Column
-------------------------------------

<div class="fixed-box">
  🔧 <a href="https://github.com/CLS-Data/mode-effects-database">Submit issues via GitHub</a>.
</div>

<h5> Introduction </h5>
<hr style="border:2px solid gray">

This searchable database contains a comprehensive collection of mode effects estimates. Here you will find mode effect estimates obtained from 90 mode experiments, identified and extracted as part of a [systematic review](https://doi.org/10.31235/osf.io/bc7qn_v1){target="_blank"} of the literature. 

This database can be used to inform future design and analysis of mixed-mode survey data. It allows users to find mode effect estimates reported in the literature for a given variable, mode comparison, and population of interest. The mode effect estimates can be used to guide survey design decisions by providing information on the risk of mode effects for different survey items and in different populations. The estimates can also be used to assess and improve the quality of mixed-mode data analysis. For example, they can be used to conduct sensitivity analyses that seek to either correct, or evaluate the implications of, bias arising from mode effects. See [Wright et al. (2024)](https://cls.ucl.ac.uk/data_documentation/handling-mode-effects-in-the-cls-cohort-studies-user-guide-nov-2024/){target="_blank"} for more details.

The mode effects have been located using a systematic search of the bibliographic databases Scopus, Embase 1974-2025, MEDLINE 1946-2025, Health and Psychosocial Instruments, APA PsycInfo, APA PsycExtra, Web of Science Core Collection (all searched in March 2025). Further searches were also conducted in Google Scholar and via a backwards and forwards citation screen process. All searches were conducted in March-April 2025; the database therefore contains mode effects published up until then.

<h5>How to use </h5>
<hr style="border:2px solid gray">

1. To use the database, navigate to the 'Mode effects' tab, where you can search for mode effect estimates based on specific item, item category, population, year of publication, country, and other details. All fields are searchable or have an available drop-down menu to make it easier to narrow down to relevant mode effects. The global search field in the top-right corner searches all fields in the database simultaneously. The custom search builder in the top-left corner allows users to build a combination of searches. For example, by combining 1) "Sub-category", "Equals", "Smoking", and 2) "Reference mode", "Contains", then typing "web", results will be filtered to those items related to smoking for which the reference mode contains 'Web'. An alternative way to search is to use the filter boxes at the top of each column, which are either free text or drop-down menus, and allow building of more complex search combinations. 

2. The 'Study details' tab contains more information about the design and reporting of each study, as well as appraisal of the quality of reporting, any relevant comments regarding selection and item non-response, as well as general comments that highlight any other relevant information. To see more details about the study from which a mode effect estimate has been obtained, the two tables can be cross-referenced using the unique ID in the first column.

*Things to note:*

• Not all relevant values were reported in all studies. Where possible, we have manually derived additional measures based on the information provided. Any values that have been derived post-hoc are presented in italics.

• Where a cell is empty, this means that no sufficient information was reported in the study to allow for direct extraction or derivation.

• Where possible, we prioritised extracting unadjusted estimates to allow consistency in comparisons across studies. However, where weighting was applied to improve sample representativeness, we prioritised the weighted estimates since they should be more generalisable to the stated target population. Further details of our extraction strategy can be seen in our [pre-registered protocol](https://osf.io/bs5dw){target="_blank"} and [pre-print](https://doi.org/10.31235/osf.io/bc7qn_v1){target="_blank"}.

<br>

<h5>How to cite </h5>
<hr style="border:2px solid gray">
Tomova GD, Silverwood RJ, Wright L. 2026. Mode effects on survey item measurement: A systematic review of the experimental evidence. SocArXiv. https://doi.org/10.31235/osf.io/bc7qn_v1 

<br>

<h5> Further resources </h5>
<hr style="border:2px solid gray">

For an accessible practice guide on when to anticipate mode effects in mixed-mode surveys, see:\
[**Tomova et al. 2026. Survey Practice Guide 8: When to anticipate mode effects in mixed-mode surveys.**](https://surveyfutures.net/practice-guides){target="_blank"}

For an intuitive introduction to mode effects using directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), see:\
[**Tomova et al. 2026. How can the use of different modes of survey data collection introduce bias? An introduction to mode effects using directed acyclic graphs (DAGs).**](https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwag017){target="_blank"}

For a detailed introduction and discussion of methods for handling mode effects, see:\
[**Wright et al. 2024. Handling Mode Effects in the CLS Cohort Studies**](https://cls.ucl.ac.uk/data_documentation/handling-mode-effects-in-the-cls-cohort-studies-user-guide-nov-2024/){target="_blank"}

Mode effects
=====================================

Column
-------------------------------------
```{r mode-effects-table}
datatable(
  mode_effects,
  container = htmltools::withTags(table(
    id = 'mode_table',
    class = 'display',
    thead(
      tr(
        # spanners
        th(colspan = 9, 'Study', style = 'text-align: center; background-color: #ddbdff;'),
        th(colspan = 4, 'Variable', style = 'text-align: center; background-color: #30d6ff;'),
        th(colspan = 2, 'Mode', style = 'text-align: center; background-color: #30d6ff;'),
        th(colspan = 2, 'Measure', style = 'text-align: center; background-color: #30d6ff;'),
        th(colspan = 10, 'Mode effect', style = 'text-align: center; background-color: #ba82ff;'), 
        th(colspan = 2, 'Sample size', style = 'text-align: center; background-color: #ddbdff;'),
      ),
tr(lapply(seq_along(names(mode_effects)), function(i) {
          col_name <- names(mode_effects)[i]
          if (i %in% c(9, 13, 15, 17, 27)) { # darker borders for these
            th(col_name, style = 'border-right: 2px solid #666;')
          } else {
            th(col_name)
          }
        })
      )
    )
  )),
  rownames = FALSE,
  extensions = c("SearchBuilder", "DateTime"),
  options = list(
    columnDefs = list(
  list(
    targets = 0,  # assumes ID is the first column
    render = JS("
      function(data, type, row, meta) {
        if (type === 'display') {
          return '<a href=\"#\" class=\"id-link\" data-id=\"' + data + '\" data-target=\"studies\">' + data + '</a>';
        }
        return data;
      }
    ")
  )
),
    dom = 'Qlfrt<"dt-bottom-left"p>',
    searchBuilder = TRUE,
    searchHighlight = TRUE,
    pageLength = 100,
    scrollY = "55vh",
    scrollCollapse = FALSE,
    scrollX = TRUE,
    # ensure search box is always fixed above table
    initComplete = JS("
      function(settings, json) {
        var api = this.api();
        var tableContainer = $(api.table().container());
        var searchBox = tableContainer.find('div.dataTables_filter');

        if (searchBox.length) {
          var wrapperId = 'searchbox-wrapper-' + settings.sInstance;
          if (!$('#' + wrapperId).length) {
            // insert a wrapper before the table
            tableContainer.before('<div id=\"' + wrapperId + '\" class=\"fixed-searchbox\"></div>');
      }
      $('#' + wrapperId).append(searchBox);
    }
  }
"),
# ensure paginator is always fixed at bottom left and showing the n of results displayed
drawCallback = JS("
  function(settings) {
    var api = this.api();
    var wrapper = $(api.table().container()); // DataTables wrapper for this table
    var $pager = wrapper.find('.dataTables_paginate');

    if ($pager.length) {
      $pager.addClass('fixed-pager');

      var infoId = 'results-info-' + settings.sInstance;
      if (!$('#' + infoId).length) {
        $pager.prepend('<span id=\"' + infoId + '\" class=\"results-info\"></span>');
      }

      var pageInfo = api.page.info();
      var filtered = pageInfo.recordsDisplay;
      var overall = pageInfo.recordsTotal;
      var showingStart = filtered === 0 ? 0 : pageInfo.start + 1;
      var showingEnd = filtered === 0 ? 0 : pageInfo.end;

      var resultsText;
      if (filtered === 0) {
        resultsText = 'No results found';
      } else {
        resultsText = 'Showing ' + showingStart + '–' + showingEnd +
                      ' of ' + filtered + ' results' +
                      (filtered !== overall ? ' (filtered from ' + overall + ')' : '');
      }

      $('#' + infoId).text(resultsText);
      
      // Add reset button with new functionality
      var resetBtnId = 'reset-btn-' + settings.sInstance;
      if (!$('#' + resetBtnId).length) {
        $pager.append('<button id=\"' + resetBtnId + '\" class=\"btn btn-light btn-sm\" style=\"margin-left: 1rem;\">Reset filters</button>');
      }
      
      // Reset button click handler - reload page and return to current tab
      $('#' + resetBtnId).off('click').on('click', function() {
        // Get the current active tab
        var activeTab = $('.navbar-nav .active a').text().trim();
        
        // Store the active tab in sessionStorage before reload
        sessionStorage.setItem('activeTab', activeTab);
        
        // Reload the page
        location.reload();
      });
    }
  }
")
),
  filter = "top",
  escape = FALSE
) %>%
  formatStyle(c("Mode effect estimate", "Standardised mode effect estimate"), backgroundColor = "#eedeff")%>%
  formatStyle(columns = c(9, 13, 15, 17, 27), `border-right` = "2px solid #666")
```

<script>
$(document).on('click', 'a.id-link', function(e) {
  e.preventDefault();
  var id = $(this).data('id');
  var target = $(this).data('target'); // "studies" or "mode"

  // decide which tab to show
  var tabText = (target === 'studies') ? 'Details of each study' : 'Mode effects';

  // click the correct tab in the navbar
  var navLink = $('.navbar-nav a').filter(function() {
    return $(this).text().trim() === tabText;
  }).first();
  if (navLink.length) navLink.click();

  // wait a moment for tab to show, then filter the right table
  setTimeout(function() {
    var tableId = (target === 'studies') ? 'studies_table' : 'mode_table';
    var dt = $('#' + tableId).DataTable();
    dt.column(0).search('^' + id + '$', true, false).draw();
    // optional scroll into view
    var pos = $('#' + tableId).offset();
    if (pos) $('html, body').animate({scrollTop: pos.top - 80}, 300);
  }, 300);
});
</script>
